title: Web UI for Virtual Models
description: Embedded Svelte SPA for managing virtual models via web browser. Provides full CRUD with a visual condition builder that adapts predicates based on metadata field types.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
A Svelte 5 SPA embedded in the Go binary via go:embed. Served by the existing chi router on the same port as the API. Uses the existing /api/v1/virtual-models REST endpoints for all operations.

Browser → GET / → SPA (index.html)
Browser → GET /api/v1/virtual-models → Go handler → SQLite
Browser → POST /api/v1/virtual-models → Go handler → SQLite

Tech: Svelte 5, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, go:embed.

sections.title: Tech Stack
sections.content:
Frontend:
- Svelte 5 (vanilla, NOT SvelteKit) for reactive UI components
- Vite as build tool (outputs to web/dist/)
- Tailwind CSS v4 for styling
- No external UI component library (custom components)

Backend Integration:
- go:embed directive in cmd/llm-router/main.go to embed web/dist/
- chi router serves SPA: index.html for non-API GET requests
- Static assets served from /assets/* path
- New endpoint: GET /api/v1/metadata/fields (returns field definitions from models.json)

Build:
- cd web && npm install && npm run build → produces web/dist/
- go build embeds web/dist/ into binary
- Single binary deployment, no separate frontend server needed

sections.title: SPA Architecture
sections.content:
Directory structure:
web/
  package.json
  vite.config.js
  svelte.config.js
  tailwind.config.js
  postcss.config.js
  index.html
  src/
    main.js
    App.svelte
    lib/
      api.js          # API client wrapping fetch calls
      stores.js        # Svelte writable stores for state
      fields.js        # Metadata field type definitions
    components/
      VirtualModelList.svelte    # List view with actions
      VirtualModelForm.svelte    # Create/edit form wrapper
      ConditionBuilder.svelte    # Filter condition builder
      SortBuilder.svelte         # Sort expression builder
      ResolvedPreview.svelte     # Shows resolved models
      FieldSelector.svelte       # Metadata field dropdown
      OperatorSelector.svelte    # Operator dropdown (type-aware)
      ValueInput.svelte          # Value input (type-aware)
      ConfirmDialog.svelte       # Delete confirmation modal
      LoginPrompt.svelte         # Admin API key input
      Toast.svelte               # Error/success notifications
    app.css           # Tailwind imports

State management via Svelte writable stores:
- virtualModels: list of all VMs
- metadataFields: field definitions from API
- selectedVM: currently editing VM (null for create)
- adminKey: API key from localStorage
- toasts: notification queue

sections.title: API Endpoints Used
sections.content:
Existing endpoints (no changes needed):
GET    /api/v1/virtual-models           → List all VMs
GET    /api/v1/virtual-models/{id}      → Get single VM
GET    /api/v1/virtual-models/{id}/resolved → Get resolved models
POST   /api/v1/virtual-models           → Create VM
PUT    /api/v1/virtual-models/{id}      → Update VM
DELETE /api/v1/virtual-models/{id}      → Delete VM

New endpoint (to be added):
GET    /api/v1/metadata/fields          → Returns field definitions

Request/Response formats remain unchanged. The SPA constructs filter_expr and sort_expr JSON matching the existing schema:

Filter: {"and": [{"key": "intelligence", "op": "gte", "value": 80}, ...]}
Sort: [{"key": "intelligence", "direction": "desc"}, ...]

Authentication: Bearer token in Authorization header, same as existing admin API. Token stored in localStorage after user enters it in login prompt.

sections.title: Condition Builder (Core UX)
sections.content:
The condition builder is the primary UX component. It renders a dynamic form for constructing filter_expr JSON.

Each condition row has 3 parts:
1. Field Selector - dropdown of available metadata fields, grouped by type:
   - Numeric: intelligence, coding, speed, hallucination, reasoning, latency, cost_per_1m_input, cost_per_1m_output, cost_per_task, context_window
   - String: cost_type
   - Boolean: has_reasoning_effort

2. Operator Selector - changes based on field type:
   - Number fields: = (eq), != (neq), > (gt), >= (gte), < (lt), <= (lte)
   - String with known values (cost_type): = (eq), != (neq), in
   - String general: = (eq), != (neq), contains
   - Boolean: = (eq), != (neq)

3. Value Input - changes based on field type + operator:
   - Number: numeric input with optional slider (min/max from field definition)
   - String with known values: dropdown for eq/neq, multi-select chips for in
   - String general: text input
   - Boolean: toggle switch (true/false)
   - in operator: multi-select chips

Features:
- Add condition button (+)
- Remove condition button (x per row)
- Visual summary: "intelligence >= 80 AND cost_type = free"
- All conditions are AND-ed (matching existing filter_expr format)

Output JSON:
{"and": [{"key": "intelligence", "op": "gte", "value": 80}, {"key": "cost_type", "op": "eq", "value": "free"}]}

sections.title: Sort Builder
sections.content:
Renders a dynamic form for constructing sort_expr JSON.

Each sort criterion row has 2 modes:

1. Direction mode (for numeric/string comparison):
   - Field selector
   - Direction toggle: ascending (asc) / descending (desc)
   - Output: {"key": "intelligence", "direction": "desc"}

2. Custom order mode (for categorical fields):
   - Field selector (limited to string fields with known values)
   - Drag-to-order list of known values
   - Output: {"key": "cost_type", "order": ["subscription", "free", "api-creds"]}

Features:
- Add sort criterion button
- Remove sort criterion button
- Drag-to-reorder sort priority (first criterion = primary sort)
- Mode toggle per row (direction vs custom order)

Output JSON (array, order matters):
[{"key": "intelligence", "direction": "desc"}, {"key": "cost_type", "order": ["subscription", "free"]}]

sections.title: Virtual Model Form
sections.content:
Create/Edit form combining all components:

Fields:
- Name (text input, required, must be unique)
- Filter conditions (ConditionBuilder component)
- Sort criteria (SortBuilder component)
- Max retries (number input, 0-3, default 0)
- Retry on status (multi-select: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504)

Behavior:
- On submit: constructs CreateVirtualModelRequest / UpdateVirtualModelRequest JSON
- POST/PUT to API
- On success: navigates back to list, shows toast
- On error: shows error toast, highlights invalid fields
- After save: shows ResolvedPreview for the saved VM

Validation:
- Name is required
- At least one filter condition recommended (but empty filter is valid = matches all)
- Filter/sort JSON validated client-side before submit

sections.title: Virtual Model List
sections.content:
Table view of all virtual models:

Columns:
- Name
- Filter summary (human-readable: "intelligence >= 80 AND cost_type = free")
- Sort summary ("intelligence desc, cost_type: [subscription, free]")
- Actions (edit, delete)

Features:
- "Create New Virtual Model" button at top
- Click row to expand inline ResolvedPreview
- Delete button shows ConfirmDialog
- Search/filter by name
- Loading skeleton while fetching

sections.title: Resolved Models Preview
sections.content:
Calls GET /api/v1/virtual-models/{id}/resolved and displays:

- Priority-ordered list of matching models
- Each entry: #position provider/model [tag1=val1, tag2=val2, ...]
- Color-coded: top priority green, fallback yellow
- Compact tag display matching TUI format: [int=85, code=78, spd=80, $/1M=2.50, hall=12]
- Empty state: "No matching models found"
- Used in:
  - Inline expansion in list view
  - Preview section in create/edit form (after save)

sections.title: Go Integration
sections.content:

3. cmd/llm-router/main.go (MODIFY)

4. architecture.json (MODIFY)

sections.title: Predicate Type Matrix
sections.content:
This matrix defines which operators and value inputs are available for each field type. It drives the condition builder's dynamic behavior.

NUMBER fields (intelligence, coding, speed, hallucination, reasoning, latency, cost_per_1m_input, cost_per_1m_output, cost_per_task, context_window):
  Operators: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte
  Value input: numeric input with optional slider (min/max from field def)

STRING with known values (cost_type: subscription, api-creds, free):
  Operators: eq, neq, in
  Value input: dropdown for eq/neq, multi-select chips for in

STRING general (any other string tag):
  Operators: eq, neq, contains
  Value input: text input

BOOLEAN (has_reasoning_effort):
  Operators: eq, neq
  Value input: toggle switch (true/false)
